svg.title: Bleeding in children decision chart: read clotting times against newborn ranges, then mucocutaneous bleeding points to immune thrombocytopenia or von Willebrand disease and deep or umbilical bleeding to hemophilia or vitamin K deficiency (hemorrhagic disease of the newborn); each column gives presentation, investigations and management

svg.text: Child who bleeds: EXCESSIVE or UNUSUAL, read against NEWBORN normals?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: excessive: nosebleed > 10 min, gum bleeding, wide bruising, heavy menses · unusual: brain or joint bleed, umbilical stump,

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif
Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: liver immature until 6 months: vitamin K factors, protein C, S low → prothrombin time (PT/INR) and activated partial

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: thromboplastin time (aPTT) normally LONGER, worst if premature

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: LIFE-THREATENING bleed, no diagnosis yet → fresh frozen plasma (most factors; little VIII, vWF, fibrinogen) · cryoprecipitate
